content.comment_body: I'm confused because the box label shows FS: 01, but the device itself offers Modbus TCP and in [product_name] Comfort [version_no] it's labeled as FS: 04. Is there a way to use the label to confirm if Modbus TCP/IP communication is available? Image label: [snip] Thanks.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. The URL you provided doesn't work. If you have the current [product_name] [version_no] (with order number [article_no]) and FS01, it should have Modbus TCP/IP capability and in hardware selection, it's listed as [product_name] FS4. However, if your device is an older [product_name] ([article_no]) with FS01, it won't support Modbus TCP/IP, only Ethernet TCP/IP with S7 protocol. In hardware selection, that's listed as [version_no] Standard.

The image shows firmware version [version_no], which confirms it's a newer model supporting Modbus TCP/IP. For programming, select [product_name] FS4 and be sure to use at least [product_name] Comfort [version_no], or update to the latest version [version_no]. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about how to determine Modbus TCP/IP support for [product_name] devices using only box label details. The discussion highlights the importance of checking firmware version, order number, and FS code, as labeling alone is unclear. This requires users to cross-check multiple sources, adding unnecessary difficulty to identifying device capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect product labels to clearly show Modbus TCP/IP support, allowing them to easily differentiate device versions and compatible communication protocols without needing further software checks or documentation.
